vedic_reference.root_origin: Shiva, Lord of Destruction and Creation
vedic_reference.note: In Hinduism, Lord Shiva is the god of destruction, who destroys the universe at the end of every cosmic period, and then recreates it. The name 'Shaambhav' is derived from 'Shiva', meaning 'The Shining God'. Shiva is also called 'Bhava' or 'Prakriti-purusha', the primal creator of the universe. The prefix 'Shaam' in the name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Sham', which means 'auspicious', 'benevolent', 'gracious', and 'shining'. Thus, the name 'Shaambhav' signifies the auspicious and gracious nature of Lord Shiva.
